column2: With a long tail: at the end of the letters he should say "encircle the enemy"; having spoken "jrimbha jrimbha" twice, the mantra ends with armour and weapon.
The mantra named Mala (garland), O best of Brahmins, has syllables arrow-eye-earth; the sage, worship and so on of the Mala mantra and the eight-syllable are as before.
Chanted, it gives victory in battle, destroys disease in illness. The mantra-knower who thus worships the son of the Wind, Lord of monkeys,
obtains all desires, even those very hard to get; wealth, grain, sons, grandsons, incomparable good fortune, fame,
intelligence, learning, splendour, kingdom, victory in dispute, the subjugating and other rites, victory in battle.
Worshipped, the son born of Anjana's womb gives abundantly.
He should worship the son of Anjana on a Shaiva or Vaishnava seat. The six-cornered figure with the six-syllable "kuta", and inside it the other (letters) written.
In the six corners he should write the six limbs with their seeds; in the middle the gentle (form) is to be written, and there worship Maruti.
The six limbs and names in the six corners as before; on the eight petals these eight monkeys are to be worshipped in order:
Sugriva, Angada, Sushena, Nala, Nila, Jambavan, Prahasta,
and Suvesha; then he should worship the deities of the six limbs: first Anjana-putra, then Rudra-murti,
then Vayu-suta, Janaki-jivana, Rama-duta, and Brahmastra-nivarana.
Having worshipped with five services, he should declare place and time, take kusha water, and recite the lamp-mantra.
Facing north, the best of practitioners accomplishes it by chanting; having chanted the mantra in the "kuta" way, he should pour the water on the ground.
Then, making his hands a cup, he should chant the mantra as able: "By this best of lamps, facing north,
do thus, Hanuman, so that my wishes are fulfilled." The thirteen materials are: cow dung, clay, soot (ink),
lac-dye, red arsenic, red sandal, sandal, honey, musk, curd, milk, butter, and ghee.
Cow dung is declared twofold, of cow and of buffalo; if the first is lost, buffalo dung is held (as substitute).
On a traveller's coming from afar, in protecting a great fort, in protecting children and the like, in destroying fear of thieves and the like,
in tasks like subduing women, cow dung is praised. What has touched the ground is not to be taken, nor what is in the air in a vessel.
Clay is fourfold: white, yellow, red, black. Among these: gopichandana, haritala (orpiment), gauri earth;
ink is made from lac-juice; all else is plain. Having made a square house with gopichandana, the wise one
should make in its middle an image of Hanuman with buffalo dung; the attentive mantra-knower should write the seed, "krodha", and its tail.
He should bathe the image with oil and mark a tilaka with jaggery; incense equal to a hundred-petalled lotus, from sal resin,
he should make an oil lamp with five wicks; the best practitioner should give an offering of curd-rice.
Three times at the throat, releasing the remaining poison. When this is done, lost buffaloes and cows,
slaves and the like that are lost are said to be regained. Against fear from thieves and wicked beings, serpents and the like,
having made a beautiful house with four doors of orpiment, an elephant should be set at the east door, a buffalo at the south,
a serpent at the west door and a tiger at the north; and thus in order sword, razor, staff and mallet.
Drawing the image in the middle with buffalo cow dung, with drum in hand and startled eyes,
bathing it with milk, anointing it with red sandal, worshipping with jasmine flowers, he should arrange pure incense,
give a lamp with ghee and offer milk-rice. He should chant "gaganam dipika-indu-adhya" and the scripture before it.
Having done this for seven days, he is freed from great fear. On Tuesday of these two, he should begin with respect.
When fear of an enemy army has come, having made a circle with red ochre, in its middle he should draw a palm tree bending as desired,
and an image hanging there with cow dung; in the left hand the palm top, in the right the knowledge-mudra.
From the root of the palm, on the road in the direction of one's own lot, a hand's breadth, having made a square house, he should draw an image in the middle,
lovely, facing south, with hands folded at the heart. He should offer water for bathing, perfume and so on as possible.
He should offer thin rice-porridge with ghee as the offering; the chant is "kili kili"; thus one does daily.
Thus done, there is soon the arrival of travellers. Writing with a piece of black stone the king's house,
a wall with four doors, at the doors of Hanuman with tails joined and three coils,
he should make an image with cow dung and worship with thorn-apple flowers, incense of jatamansi, a lamp of ghee smeared with oil;
the offering is a black-gram cake with sesame oil and alkali. He should be meditated on eating the cake with the right hand;
with the left hand frightening the enemy soldiers with stones, crushing them, standing with frowning brow, terrifying and churning.
Absorbed in meditation he should chant "bhug bhug" a thousand times. By this procedure he destroys the enemy army,
and there is protection of fortresses, true, true, without doubt. There are many applications; I have told them in brief.
He who daily offers a lamp to Hanuman by rule — for him nothing in the three worlds is impossible.
It should not be given to one of wicked heart, of wicked thought, to an ill-mannered disciple, to a slanderer,
nor to an ungrateful man; it should be given to the tested. What more need be said? The Lord of monkeys gives everything.
Now I shall tell another mantra, giving knowledge of truth: Om, "namo Hanumate", he should say "jatharatraya",
danakshobha he should say, "samhara samhara", then "atmatattvam prakashaya prakashaya",
ending with armour, weapon and "svaha": a mantra of twenty-six and a half syllables. Its sage is Vasishtha; the metre is Anushtubh; the deity again:
Hanuman; with syllables sage-seven-seasons-Veda-eight-scriptures in order, having made the six limbs, he should meditate on the Lord of monkeys:
his left arm on his knee, in the knowledge-mudra at his heart, seated, mind on the Self, in the midst of a plantain grove,
like ten million rising suns: he should meditate on Hari, giver of knowledge. Having meditated thus he should chant a hundred thousand and offer a tenth with sesame,
with ghee, and worship the Lord on the seat stated before. Chanted, it surely destroys the agitation of love.
By the grace of the Lord of monkeys he obtains knowledge of truth. Now I shall tell another mantra, supreme at driving off spirits:
Om, the "Kashi" seed, "Varaha" above, "Anjana", "Pavana", "Vanaputra" at the end, "aveshaya aveshaya" twice he should say;
Om, "Shri Hanumate", the arrow-cha-arms syllables. Brahma is the sage, Gayatri the metre, the deity again:
Hanuman; Kamala the seed; "phat" the power. With the seed rich in six long vowels he should perform the six limbs.
The best practitioner should meditate on Anjaneya, red-faced, with a body like a golden mountain, sitting at the foot of the parijata tree.
Having meditated thus, he should chant a hundred thousand and offer a tenth part with sesame; the wise one should worship as before on the seat stated before, with three sweet things.
With this mantra the practitioner should wipe a person seized by a planet; crying out, he is freed and the planet quickly flees.
These mantras are to be always kept secret and not disclosed anywhere; they should be given to a tested disciple or to one's own son.
The wise, devoted to the worship of Hanuman, having especially worshipped Kartavirya Arjuna as stated, obtains the fruit.
Dashasya and so on: the six limbs with six words in the dative. He should meditate on the intoxicated best of kings sprinkled by young women, sporting in the water of the Narmada,
stopping the flood of water with his hands. Having thus meditated, he should chant ten thousand; the rest as before.
First he should chant a hundred thousand, and the worship and application are as before. "King Kartavirya Arjuna of a thousand arms":
by merely remembering him one says that what is stolen and lost is regained. This best mantra is had of thirty-two syllables.
The five limbs are with all the feet; meditation, worship and so on as before. After "Kartaviryaya" he should say "vidmahe";
after "Mahaviryaya" he should say "dhimahi"; "Tan no Arjunah", at the end "prachodayat" he should say.
This is said to be the Gayatri of Arjuna; one should chant it at the start of the practice. For those who chant the Anushtubh mantra at night, gatherings of thieves
flee far from the house, by tarpana and by the sound. Now I shall tell the lamp rite, dear to Kartavirya:
one should begin the lamp in Vaishakha, Shravana, Margashirsha, Kartika, Ashvina, Pausha, Magha and Phalguna months;
on a tithi free of Rikta, on a day other than Saturday and Tuesday, under Hasta, Uttara, Ashvini, Mrigashira, Pushya, Shravana, Svati,
Vishakha, and Rohini, the beginning of the lamp brings benefit; at the Vyatipata end, in Dhriti, Vriddhi, Sukarma,
Priti, Harsha, Saubhagya, Shobhana, and Ayushmat; in a karana free of Vishti, at an eclipse, in half-risings and so on,
in yogas, at night or forenoon, the beginning of the lamp is auspicious. On the bright seventh of Kartika at midnight it is exceedingly auspicious;
if Sunday or the Shravana star falls there, it is hard to get. For very necessary tasks, the purification of months and the like is not needed.
On the first day, fasting, self-restrained, celibate, in yellow clothes, bathed in the morning, on pure ground plastered with cow dung and water,
having done pranayama and resolve, he should do the placings stated before. On the ground he should draw a six-cornered figure with red sandal and rice-grains.
Then drawing Smara (Kama) he should write in the six corners; enclose it with the nine syllables; outside it a triangle again.
In the yantra so drawn he should place the lamp-vessel, made of gold, silver or copper, in absence of those
of bell-metal or clay, of iron for the lowest; in calamity; for peace, a vessel of mung flour; in a junction, one of wheat flour.
For a thousand palas of ghee, the vessel is a hundred palas; for ten thousand palas of ghee, the vessel is five hundred palas;
for seventy-five, the vessel is sixty palas; for three thousand palas of ghee, a vessel of sugar palas;
for two to three thousand, a vessel of two hundred; for a hundred, thus for the other counts one should arrange.
For a daily lamp, a fire-pala; the vessel and ghee a pala is remembered. Having set the vessel so, he should put in wicks made of thread:
one, three, or five, seven and so on, odd; the number of strands is made according to the tithi, up to a thousand.
There he should put cow ghee purified with clean cloth: a thousand palas and so on, the tenth part by the weight of the task.
A lovely rod of gold and the like, sixteen finger-breadths long, or half or half of that, fine at the tip and thick at the root,
he should release in the middle of the vessel at the right, with its tip pointed, leaving four finger-breadths to the right of the vessel;
he should plant an auspicious knife pointed downward, held on the right. There he should light the lamp preceded by remembering Ganesha.
East of the lamp, in an all-auspicious diagram or in an eight-petalled rice figure, he should establish a pot by rule.
Invoking the lord of kings there, the wise one should worship as before. Taking water and rice-grains he should make the resolve for the lamp.
This lamp-resolve mantra is told from "dvishu-bhumi": Om, Pasha, Maya, the tuft, the "karta" syllables,
viryarjunaya Mahishmatinathaya sahasra, at the end of "bahave", he should say "sahasra";
kratudikshitahastaya Dattatreyapriyaya Atreyaya Anasuya-garbha-ratnaya:
namo ... "this lamp accept, protect so-and-so, protect, protect;
destroy the wicked, destroy, throw down, strike, slay the enemies, slay"; Maya, Om, own seed, the self-born (Kama):
vahnipriya (svaha). "By this best lamp, facing west, protect so-and-so; at the end of so-and-so, O giver of boons":
(coded syllables of the Chamunda seed; ending with "svaha" and "pusa-bindu"):
Om, Agnipriya — a mantra of arrow-eye-earth syllables. The sage of the Mala mantra is declared Dattatreya;
the metre is boundless; Kartavirya Arjuna is the deity who accomplishes all. With Chamunda, with six long vowels, he should perform the six limbs.
Having meditated on the god and chanted the mantra, at the end he should pour water. "Govinda-adhya, plough, moon, the Chamunda seed" is declared.
Then before it he should chant the nine-syllable mantra a thousand times. Om, Ananta with bindu, Maya, own seed with left eye;
Kurma-agni with Shanti-bindu, Vahnijaya (svaha), goad, Dhruva. The sage is as before; the metre Anushtubh; the rest as before.
Having chanted this king of mantras a thousand times, he should recite the armour. The one who gives a lamp thus obtains all he desires.
At the time of awakening the lamp one should avoid inauspicious speech. The sight of a Brahmin there is declared auspicious;
for Shudras, middling; for a mleccha, killing and binding; the sight of a mouse or owl is bad; of a cow or horse, giving ease.
An even flame is for success; a crooked one makes night; a sound causes fear for the doer; a bright one is held to give happiness;
a black one produces fear from enemies; a spitting one destroys animals. When, after the lamp is lit, the vessel is seen broken by fate,
within a fortnight the sacrificer would go to Yama's abode. If the wick is changed, the task is accomplished with delay;
if a second lamp is made inside it, the doer would lose his sight. On touching impurity, disease; on the lamp's going out, fear of thieves;
on contact with a dog, cat or rat, fear from the king. A lamp made with the vessel of eight palas gives all desires.
Therefore the lamp is to be carefully guarded from obstacles. Till the end he should keep celibacy and sleep on the ground;
he should avoid even speaking with women, Shudras, outcastes and the like. He should chant the nine-syllable king of mantras a thousand times each day,
and recite the hymn each day, especially at night. He who stands on one foot before the lamp and chants the lord of mantras
a thousand times at night soon obtains his desire. Having concluded on an auspicious day, feeding the best Brahmins,
he should chant the mantra while sprinkling the doer with pot-water. The doer should give an abundant fee to please (the teacher).
When the teacher is pleased, King Kartavirya's son gives the desired. By the teacher's order he himself may do it or have the teacher do it,
giving the teacher wealth and so on for the lamp-gift, O Narada. One who makes a lamp for his own aim without the teacher's order
does not succeed; loss comes at every step. Cow ghee is declared best; buffalo ghee middling;
sesame oil likewise; ghee of goat and the like lowest. For a mouth disease, he should give a lamp of sweet-smelling oil;
for the destruction of enemies, by the lamp of ghee of a thousand palas made by "siddhartha"; ...
the doer who has accomplished his task should perform the lamp rite three times; then even a very difficult task is accomplished, without doubt.
Kartavirya is fond of lamps, the Sun fond of salutation, Mahavishnu fond of praise, Ganesha fond of ...
Durga fond of worship, Shiva fond of bathing: therefore for their satisfaction one should perform each with respect.

May the lord of heroes protect my shanks; may Manojava protect my feet; may the bearer of all weapons protect my whole body at all vital points;
naradapuran:76:41	may the destroyer of all the wicked protect my body of eight constituents; may he who grants all desired by the good protect the ten life-breaths and the lord of life;
naradapuran:76:42	may he whose host of senses is subdued protect all my senses. Whatever place is not mentioned, in the body inside or out,
naradapuran:76:43	may all that be protected for me by the lord of the lords of all worlds. This body, stronger than the thunderbolt, covered by the armour,
naradapuran:76:44	freed from a hundred afflictions, fearless — let it be mine. I have tied on this divine, impenetrable armour of the lord of the Haihayas;
naradapuran:76:45	I move day and night with a fearless heart: on the royal road, in a great fortress, on roads thick with thieves,
naradapuran:76:46	in rough places, in dreadful woods, in forest-fire, in mountain caves, in battle, among clashing weapons, in places frequented by lions and tigers,
naradapuran:76:47	in thickets, in crowded places, at twilight, in the king's court, in dispute, in great whirlpools, in the ocean, on the riverbank,
naradapuran:76:48	in a region full of highwaymen, a country thronged by robbers, when all possessions are being seized, when there is danger to life,
naradapuran:76:49	in the grip of various diseases and fevers, in torment by ghouls and spirits, in plague and bad-dream afflictions, in affliction, in breach of trust,
naradapuran:76:50	in great bodily pain and in mental fever, in fear of mental and bodily illness, in obstructions and flaming calamities,
naradapuran:76:51	let no fear whatever come to me, who am covered by the armour. May he keep off all those who come wishing to plunder our wealth,
naradapuran:76:52	the great chariot-fighter, with his thousand arms; may he make powerless of motion those hard to conquer, bound by the thousand nooses raised in his own hands;
naradapuran:76:53	may Kritavirya's son break them with the thousand goads and hacked with a thousand arrows; may the crest-jewel of kings quickly make our opponents such;
naradapuran:76:54	may he make hosts of thieves and wicked beings cut with a thousand swords and crushed by a thousand pestles, the lotus-eyed one;
naradapuran:76:55	may he who holds a thousand spokes (discus), the very incarnation of Hari, protect all of mine, terrified by the sound of his own conch.
naradapuran:76:56	O Kartavirya, great in valour, destroyer of all the wicked, everywhere, always, destroy the wicked thieves for destruction.
naradapuran:76:57	Why do you sleep, destroyer of the wicked? Why do you stay? You are slow. Arise; protect us from all fears as you would your own sons.
naradapuran:76:58	The thieves who steal wealth, the haters and the violent,
naradapuran:76:59	those who frighten the good, the deceitful, those of evil intent, the evil-hearted, wicked kings and wicked ministers and sinners,
naradapuran:76:60	those who spoil our tasks, the wicked obstructers, those who rob everything, the five deceivers and others,
naradapuran:76:61	mlecchas, bandits and outcastes who cause great trouble, arsonists, poisoners, cheats, weapon-bearers,
naradapuran:76:62	sinners, doers of wicked deeds, givers of pain, those of wicked mind, tricksters, those addicted to bad paths, and givers of many fears —
